label: workaround-needs-tracking
name: A workaround for an unexplained defect lands with no ticket, a test makes it permanent with no TODO, or a hardware workaround may be obsolete
description: What breaks: the workaround outlives its reason. A reversed free-list push order described as 'workaround for an unidentified bug' with no story id (3227447122 'do we have a ticket/story tracking this for follow up?'); a TEST_CASE that pins that ordering as a contract (3227468540 'are we enshrining this work-around forever? ... call that out here with a TODO'); clear_kv_hbm zeroing KV HBM for NaN garbage that the 'NaN-fixed' bitfile should make unnecessary (2948238427, harmless to keep, Wade's own to-do). Procedure: grep added comments, commit messages and test headers for workaround, unidentified, unknown bug, hang, hack, TODO without an id; require a ticket id next to the workaround and a TODO in any test that guards it; when the repository or PR mentions a newer hardware/bitfile version ask whether the workaround can be gated or dropped. Contrast with code-comment-carries-no-lasting-fact: he wants the tracking item to exist and a TODO in the test, but no 'Story N' in an explanatory comment (3350285744); the distinction is whether the comment marks temporary behavior.
disposition_reason: Count 3 over 2 PRs; keyword scan plus missing-id check is mechanical.
agent_feasibility: yes for the keyword scan and the missing-id check; obsolescence after a hardware fix needs domain knowledge.

members.concern: A code comment in expand() (the function that adds a hugepage chunk to the pool) describes a reversed free-list push order as a 'workaround for an unidentified bug' (first FPGA DMA hangs when the descriptor ring lands at a high offset); Wade asks whether a ticket or story tracks the follow-up investigation.

detection.trigger: An added comment or commit message contains a word such as 'workaround', 'unidentified', 'unknown bug', 'open question', 'follow-up', 'TODO' with no ticket id (STORY-nnn, issue #nnn) in the same comment block.
detection.procedure: grep the diff's added lines for workaround|unidentified|unknown|open question|follow-up|TODO|FIXME; for each hit, check the same comment block, the PR body and the commit message for a ticket reference (STORY-, #nnn, notion.so link); if none, ask for one.
detection.question: Does a ticket or story exist, and is its id written next to the workaround so the next reader can find the follow-up?

members.quote: do we have a ticket/story tracking this for follow up?
members.note: The hunk's own text supplies the trigger: 'Reproducible workaround for an unidentified bug' and 'See TODO: open question for follow-up' with no ticket id. Author answered STORY-445 and commit e4c4f49452 added 'TODO(STORY-445)' to the guarding test in t/t_heap_v2.cpp (the expand() comment in src/system/heap_v2.cpp was not changed by that commit).

members.concern: A new TEST_CASE 'expand: first allocation comes from the lowest-offset hugepage' pins the workaround ordering as a tested contract; Wade asks whether that makes the workaround permanent or whether a story will pursue the root cause, and if so asks for a TODO in the test saying so.

detection.trigger: A new test unit whose header comment says it 'guards' or 'protects' a workaround, hack, or unexplained behavior (words: workaround, hang, unidentified, silently flipped).
detection.procedure: Read the TEST_CASE header comment and the production comment it cites; check whether either names a ticket or a plan to replace the test once the root cause is known; if not, ask whether the behavior is meant to be permanent and request a TODO(ticket) in the test.
detection.question: Is this test guarding a contract the team wants forever, or a temporary workaround that a ticket will remove, and does the test text say which?

members.quote: so are we enshrining this work-around forever? Or will be create a story to pursue/understand/address it further? If so we should probably call that out here with a TODO or something.
members.note: Related to check 1 in theme (a test row with no consumer beyond the test comment) but the trigger differs: this is an ordering assertion on a free-list head, not a numeric conversion row, and Wade's remedy is a TODO plus a tracking story rather than dropping the row. Author agreed ('the output of that work will be to put in a real test for the condition and remove this one') and commit e4c4f49452 added the TODO(STORY-445) block to this test.

members.concern: The test helper clear_kv_hbm zeroes KV HBM before a test to work around NaN garbage from older FPGA bitfiles; Wade notes the 'NaN-fixed' bitfile should make it unnecessary, says leaving it is harmless, and records a to-do for himself to revisit.

detection.trigger: The diff keeps or extends a helper whose name or comment marks it as a workaround for a hardware or firmware defect (clear, zero, scrub, workaround, NaN), and the repository or PR mentions a newer hardware/bitfile version that fixes the defect.
detection.procedure: grep the test and h/ for the helper and any TRON_*_WORKAROUND macro or bitfile-version note (git grep -n 'NaN\|WORKAROUND' HEAD -- t h); read the commit list for a version mention ('No longer necessary with 1.5.7.0'); check whether the helper is gated by the workaround macro or runs unconditionally.
detection.question: Is this helper a workaround for a defect the current hardware or firmware no longer has, and if so is it gated so it can be dropped?

members.quote: I'm really hoping that with the 'NaN-fixed' bitfile, we don't need this 'clear_kv_hbm' anymore. No harm it leaving it, but I have a to-do to circle back and see if we can skip this. Once things settle ;-p...
members.note: Author: 'fixed in commit 958e77d91' = 'Gate clear_kv_hbm behind TRON_NAN_FPGA_WORKAROUND'. Verified at 429249ead6 t/t_hwattention.cpp:63 `#ifndef TRON_NAN_FPGA_WORKAROUND` around clear_kv_hbm and :545-547 around its call. Related commit in the same PR: 'remove shard::zero_v_hbm. No longer necessary with 1.5.7.0' (bitfile version). Form: Wade states a hope and a personal to-do, not an ask; the author still acted on it.

codex_bullets.bullet: Check how numerical comparisons handle not-a-number and infinite values. A tolerance check must not silently treat an invalid result as a successful comparison.
codex_bullets.reason: Two direct comments (PRs 1997, 4557). Claude check 1 and setup step 2 cite the NaN rule for value rows only; a NaN-aware comparison helper (the 1997 case) has no check.

codex_bullets.bullet: Prefer the closest existing test suite. A temporary workaround's regression test needs a documented reason and a replacement condition; do not remove protection before the underlying failure is understood.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4265, 4128, 2713, 2872). The workaround-needs-a-tracked-exit rule (2713, two comments) is new to the Claude skill.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (setup 2 quotes AGENTS.md "extend the closest existing test"; the workaround sentence has no check)
